title: Separable equations and particular solutions
objective: Solve a first-order differential equation with separable variables, and use an initial condition to find its particular solution.

blocks.text: A first-order differential equation can be written F(x, y, dy/dx) = 0 or dy/dx = f(x, y). The simplest kind has separable variables: the right-hand side is a product g(x)h(y) of a function of x alone and a function of y alone.
To solve it, separate the variables, with everything in y on one side and everything in x on the other, then integrate both sides. One constant of integration, c, is enough.

A solution that contains an arbitrary constant is the general solution. When more information is given, such as the value of y for one value of x (an initial condition), the constant can be found, and substituting it gives the particular solution. A differential equation with an initial condition is an initial value problem.

An initial value problem dy/dx = p(x)y, y(x₀) = y₀ has one and only one solution on a given interval, so a particular solution can be checked by substituting it into the equation and into the initial condition.
